scope: Archive leaderboard API, public identity directory, matching RPC allowlist; preserve all economy reducers and payment service
ordered_steps: Fetch and hash-pin live manifest, changed backend files, Nginx route and database function metadata immediately before staging.
Back up the database, current managed source and Nginx configuration outside the immutable release; verify successful backup before writes.

Clone the live release, apply only the new leaderboard module, exact handler patch and exact two-signature postgres.py patch; leave archive_backend/service.py, bundles, business CSVs and cash service unchanged.
Prepare rollback code from the old business release with the new PostgreSQL RPC allowlist retained; after SQL GRANT the unpatched old client will reject the extra executable functions.

Run rolled-back SQL fixtures and old-API privilege checks as the real application role. Check table RLS, no direct table privilege, explicit SECURITY DEFINER search_path, two new RPCs only and all old RPCs still callable.
Stage and validate the archive-only Nginx route addition, preserving authentication, IP restrictions, limits and payment routes.
Briefly stop the archive API before committing SQL grants: the old running RPC client must never serve after its allowlist becomes incompatible.
Commit only additive identity schema, seed and trigger, safe integer helper, read and bind functions; keep all existing account archives, revisions, rewards, orders and balances identical.
Atomically switch to the staged matching code, start the archive API, validate readiness and authenticated endpoint, then reload only the validated Nginx route configuration if needed.
On failure switch to the prepared old-business/new-allowlist rollback release. Preserve committed additive schema and identity rows; do not restore an old full database over real player activity.

Verify unchanged bundle hash and payment catalog, old profile/authentication endpoints, top 100 ordering, anonymous historical entries, own-row highlight metadata, unchanged-revision response and no real order or fixture row created.
acceptance_boundaries: Ranking is permanent account archive data, including in pure matches; projected current-match deltas are not used.
Every response contains at most 100 public rows and no private HMAC, save, baseline, balances or purchase history.
Names and avatars resolve through native Steam panels; historical accounts without reversible identity remain anonymous until a trusted login binds identity.
Payment test/reset permission does not exclude a real player from rankings.
Top three are pinned visually but retain authoritative rank changes; no frozen permanent winners.
UI changes only when public row/rank data or the current player's listed status changes; request timestamps are not part of the revision.
